text: By Listen (2 min) Pilgrim CEO Jake Adler soldering a circuit board. Pilgrim Inc. Two Anthropic leaders are investing in a small startup backed by Peter Thiel that is developing hardware to detect viruses in the air, as fears grow that artificial-intelligence systems might cause novel biological threats. Logan Graham, head of Anthropic’s frontier red team and Sholto Douglas, a member of its technical staff, invested in a $25 million seed round for Redwood City-Calif.-based Pilgrim that valued it at $150 million, the company said. They invested in a personal capacity along with Coinbase co-founder Fred Ehrsam , among other technology leaders, in a round led by venture capital firm Buckley Ventures.
